meta.title: CBSE Grade 5 Mathematics — Final Model Question Paper
meta.subject: Mathematics
instructions: Read each question carefully before answering.
Marks are indicated against each question.

sections.title: Section A – Multiple Choice Questions
sections.instruction: Choose the correct option. Each question carries 1 mark.

questions.question: The value of 3 + 4 × 5 − 2 using BODMAS is:
Which of the following is an improper fraction?
questions.explanation: An improper fraction has numerator ≥ denominator. 9/4 has numerator 9 > denominator 4, so it is improper. (5/5 = 1, a whole number.)

questions.question: Convert 2 3/5 into an improper fraction.
What is 25% of 200?
A trader bought an article for Rs. 480 and sold it for Rs. 600. What is his profit percentage?
Find the area of a square with side 13 cm.
questions.explanation: Area of square = side × side = 13 × 13 = 169 sq cm.

questions.question: The volume of a cuboid with length 5 cm, breadth 4 cm, and height 3 cm is:
questions.explanation: Volume of cuboid = l × b × h = 5 × 4 × 3 = 60 cubic centimetres.
Multiplying by 10 shifts the decimal point one place to the right: 0.45 × 10 = 4.5.

questions.question: Which polygon has exactly 5 sides?
questions.explanation: A pentagon has exactly 5 sides. Hexagon = 6, Quadrilateral = 4, Octagon = 8.

questions.question: In a pie chart, if a sector represents 90° out of 360°, what percentage of the total does it represent?

sections.title: Section B – Fill in the Blanks
sections.instruction: Fill in the blanks with the correct answer. Each question carries 1 mark.

questions.question: The product of 2/3 and 3/5 is ______.
questions.explanation: (2/3) × (3/5) = (2×3)/(3×5) = 6/15 = 2/5 (simplified by dividing numerator and denominator by 3).
Dividing by a fraction means multiplying by its reciprocal: 4 ÷ 1/2 = 4 × 2/1 = 8.

questions.question: 45/100 written as a decimal is ______.
A shopkeeper sells a bag for Rs. 350 that cost him Rs. 400. His loss is Rs. ______.
questions.explanation: Loss = Cost Price − Selling Price = 400 − 350 = Rs. 50.

questions.question: Principal = Rs. 5,000, Rate = 10% per annum, Time = 2 years. Simple Interest = Rs. ______.
The perimeter of an equilateral triangle with side 9 cm is ______ cm.
questions.explanation: Perimeter of equilateral triangle = 3 × side = 3 × 9 = 27 cm.

questions.question: The number of degrees in a complete turn (full rotation) is ______.
questions.explanation: A full rotation or complete turn measures 360°.
3.6 ÷ 0.4 = 36 ÷ 4 = 9 (multiply both numerator and denominator by 10 to remove decimals).

questions.question: A pattern that can be folded so both halves match exactly is said to have ______ symmetry.
questions.explanation: When a figure can be folded along a line so the two halves match exactly, it has line symmetry (also called bilateral or reflective symmetry).

questions.question: Express 3/4 as a percentage: ______.

sections.title: Section C – Short Answer Questions
sections.instruction: Answer the following questions. Each question carries 2 marks. Show your working clearly.

questions.question: Add the mixed fractions: 3 2/7 + 1 4/7.
Multiply: 4/5 × 25.
Find the area and perimeter of a rectangle with length 16 cm and breadth 9 cm.
questions.working:
Area = length × breadth = 16 × 9 = 144 sq cm
Perimeter = 2 × (length + breadth) = 2 × (16 + 9) = 2 × 25 = 50 cm

questions.question: A box is 8 cm long, 5 cm wide, and 4 cm high. Find its volume.
questions.working:
Volume of cuboid = l × b × h
= 8 × 5 × 4
= 40 × 4
= 160 cubic centimetres

questions.question: Kavya scored 72 marks out of 90 in a test. What is her percentage score?
Ramesh borrowed Rs. 8,000 from a bank at 6% per annum simple interest for 3 years. Find the total amount he has to repay.
Perform the operation: 5.84 − 2.67.
questions.working:
5.84
− 2.67
------
  3.17
(Align decimal points. Units: 4 − 7, borrow → 14 − 7 = 7. Tenths: 7 − 1 − 6 = 0, borrow → 17 − 1 − 6 = 10, write 0 carry. Ones: 4 − 1 − 2 = 1, Tens: 5 − 2 = 3. Err — re-working:
5.84 − 2.67: Hundredths: 4 < 7, borrow: 14 − 7 = 7. Tenths: 7 − 1 = 6, 6 < 6... 6 = 6, so 6 − 6 = 0. Wait: 5.84 − 2.67:
Hundredths: 4 − 7, borrow → 14 − 7 = 7
Tenths: 8 − 1(borrowed) = 7, 7 − 6 = 1
Ones: 5 − 2 = 3
Answer: 3.17)

questions.question: A trader bought 50 pens at Rs. 12 each and sold them at Rs. 15 each. Find his profit or loss percentage.
questions.working:
CP per pen = Rs. 12, SP per pen = Rs. 15
Profit per pen = 15 − 12 = Rs. 3
Profit% = (Profit / CP) × 100
= (3 / 12) × 100
= 25%

questions.question: Find the area of a right-angled triangle with base 12 cm and height 9 cm.
questions.working:
Area of triangle = (1/2) × base × height
= (1/2) × 12 × 9
= (1/2) × 108
= 54 sq cm

questions.question:
A bar graph shows the favourite fruit of 60 students. Mango: 20, Apple: 15, Banana: 10, Grapes: 15.
(a) What fraction of students like mango?
(b) What percentage like banana?
questions.working:
(a) Students who like mango = 20 out of 60
Fraction = 20/60 = 1/3

(b) Students who like banana = 10 out of 60
Percentage = (10/60) × 100 = 1000/60 = 16.67% (approx.)
Note: If total is 60 and 10 like banana, percentage = 50/3 ≈ 16.7%

sections.title: Section D – Long Answer Questions
sections.instruction: Answer the following questions. Each question carries 5 marks. Show all steps clearly.

questions.question:
A shopkeeper bought 45 kg of rice at Rs. 32 per kg and 30 kg of wheat at Rs. 24 per kg. He sold all the rice at Rs. 40 per kg and all the wheat at Rs. 28 per kg.
(a) Find the total cost price.
(b) Find the total selling price.
(c) Find the profit or loss.
(d) Find the profit or loss percentage.
questions.answer:
(a) Total CP = Rs. 2,160
(b) Total SP = Rs. 2,640
(c) Profit = Rs. 480
(d) Profit% = 22.22% (approx.)

questions.question:
Sita has a rectangular garden of length 24 m and breadth 18 m.
(a) Find the perimeter of the garden.
(b) Find the area of the garden.
(c) She wants to fence the garden on all four sides. Fencing costs Rs. 35 per metre. Find the total cost of fencing.
(d) She also wants to plant grass in the garden. Grass costs Rs. 12 per square metre. Find the total cost of planting grass.
questions.answer:
(a) Perimeter = 84 m
(b) Area = 432 sq m
(c) Cost of fencing = Rs. 2,940
(d) Cost of grass = Rs. 5,184
questions.working:
(a) Perimeter = 2 × (length + breadth)
= 2 × (24 + 18)
= 2 × 42
= 84 m

(b) Area = length × breadth
= 24 × 18
= 432 sq m

(c) Cost of fencing = Perimeter × cost per metre
= 84 × 35
= Rs. 2,940

(d) Cost of grass = Area × cost per sq m
= 432 × 12
= Rs. 5,184
